claim: Worked examples beat problem solving on a less structured task (legal-case reasoning) for first-year law students: 58.63 vs 8.59 on a 0-100 test, f=1.24, in about half the learning time.
agent_test: Give the agent a solved analogous case for open tasks versus solving cold; compare quality at equal total tokens.

claim: No expertise reversal appeared in advanced (third-year) law students: examples still beat solving (82.28 vs 37.06, f=1.02), despite prior-knowledge d=2.75. Authors blame unautomatable variable elements. Small n (9 per cell).
agent_test: Check on a strong model whether a worked example still helps on open tasks, or whether it should be dropped as capability rises.

claim: A generic list of process steps (Toulmin checklist) without worked-out solutions did not improve novice learning and added time (1460 s vs 832 s; score 8.33 vs 8.88). A checklist is not a substitute for a worked case.
agent_test: Compare checklist-only prompt, one worked case, and both at equal tokens on open tasks.

claim: In ill-structured domains the worked-example benefit grows as learner knowledge falls (essay writing, design history, music, argumentation). Support is mostly from one lab group (Sweller/Kalyuga/Renkl) and several sources were only read as abstracts or second-hand.
agent_test: Measure benefit of an example by task novelty to the model (known vs unfamiliar domain); expect benefit to fall when the model already knows the domain.

claim: Examples for ill-structured content work only when prompts direct attention to the principle (skill) rather than the topic; topic-directed prompts and topic gap-filling hurt, and low topic knowledge gives poor results.
agent_test: Annotate worked cases with the named heuristic step; compare with annotation about the content topic.

claim: Self-explanation prompts added to instruction did not help transfer on semi-structured reasoning tasks (N=79, delayed test); prompt benefits are not universal.
agent_test: Test forced self-explanation step versus none on reasoning items at equal tokens.

claim: Chain-of-thought (written-out reasoning) gives large gains on math (+12.3), symbolic (+14.2) and logic (+6.9) but near none elsewhere (56.8 vs 56.1); on MMLU about 95% of gain is on questions with an equals sign. Verified in the paper text.
agent_test: Route: use stepwise reasoning only for symbolic/computational subproblems; run an equal-token direct baseline on soft tasks.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: A symbolic solver or tool beats CoT execution on math and logic; CoT gain is mostly from carrying out steps, not planning.
agent_test: Plan then call a tool or code versus plan then CoT at equal tokens.

claim: Forced deliberation can hurt: implicit statistical learning drops (GPT-4o 87.5 to 64.4 with CoT; o1-preview 57.7 vs 94.0 GPT-4o on a 440 subset), also face recognition and exception-laden labels. Verified in the paper. Gap search 2025-2026: no study re-tests implicit statistical learning in o1/R1-class models; harm from more thinking appears on distractor and instruction-following tasks (d01, d02), not shown for implicit learning itself.
agent_test: Include tasks where pattern perception dominates and test fast-answer path versus deliberate path.

claim: Demonstrations in classification help mainly by showing label space, input distribution and format; correct labels matter little. Examples act as format cues.
agent_test: Replace example content with format-only scaffold and compare.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: More similar or relevant context can lower quality on hard, novel open-form questions (GPT-4, 160 questions), while it helps closed-form benchmarks.
agent_test: Retrieve near examples versus distant or none for open tasks; plot quality against similarity.

claim: Many-shot prompting gains are task-dependent: large for structured, constrained-output tasks, small for open generation; reinforced and unsupervised ICL can match human solutions; accuracy can fall after about 125 shots and order changes results by 2-3 points or more.
agent_test: Cap examples at a few, test order shuffles, report variance.

claim: Example-based and AI-assisted support in open creative work narrows output: GenAI images raise design fixation (+0.32, BF 124), ChatGPT ideation homogenizes groups (d=.47), feedback-tuned models lower essay diversity, chat templates collapse diversity.
agent_test: For open mode, generate in parallel without shared examples, then compare diversity at equal tokens.

claim: Structure in the request (population-referential instruction, direction stratification, verbalized sampling) restores diversity without examples: VS 1.6-2.1x diversity, +25.7% human rating, 66.8% of base diversity recovered (verified). Gap search: NoveltyBench found sequential in-context regeneration (previous outputs shown) matches human diversity at higher token cost; system-prompt creativity requests only marginal (d09).
agent_test: Compare example-free diversification prompts with example-fed generation per 100k tokens.

claim: Models and humans use fewer reasoning elements on ill-structured problems; models accuracy 62.4% well, 51.7% intermediate, 57.5% ill. Guidance by successful-trace order helped ill-structured most (+9.7, dilemmas +18.8) but only for strong models; weak models lost up to 13.1.
agent_test: Gate scaffold intensity on model strength; test on ill-structured items with strong and weak model.

claim: Worked-step prompts in planning generalize poorly: gains only when example class matches the test class and fall as problem size grows (Blocksworld GPT-4 3.83 to 59.3 with specific CoT).
agent_test: Test scaffold on out-of-distribution problem size.

claim: Heuristic-classification prompting on ill-structured induction tasks gains little over strong baselines at lower tokens than tree search (24 Game: 36.49% at 2.88M tokens vs ToT-BFS 55.65% at 7.28M); on 1D-ARC it helped a strong model slightly and hurt a weaker one.
agent_test: Equal-token comparison of pattern-listing scaffold vs search.

claim: No direct replication, failed replication or LLM worked-example study in ill-structured tasks was found for Nievelstein 2013; one reanalysis (N=74) found worked-example effect on self-explanation not significant, and benefits moderated by shifting ability and fluid intelligence. Gap search: a citation scan of 93 citing records found no replication; near-domain studies (apprentice diagnosis n=78 and n=118) give a null and a partial effect (unaided skill not improved).
agent_test: Run the first LLM worked-example test on open tasks ourselves.

claim: Reasoning models are not immune to harm from extra thinking or from examples: accuracy falls with longer reasoning on distractor, spurious-feature and deduction tasks; explicit CoT lowers instruction-following in 13 of 14 models (Llama3-8B 75.2 to 59.0); few-shot CoT lowers reasoning-model accuracy and gets worse with more exemplars. But on math, CoT or one-shot CoT still helps R1-distilled models in 72% of cells. So the effect depends on task and model.
agent_test: Run the open-mode tasks with thinking off, short, and long; compare quality and repetition at equal tokens.

claim: Gating whether to reason is feasible but not solved for task type: a model's own judgement has high recall and low precision; a trained per-model classifier (validation accuracy 0.75-0.92) recovers most lost accuracy; difficulty routers exist. No published gate separates well- from ill-structured tasks, and no study measures the misrouting cost for that split.
agent_test: Build a small labelled set of structured vs open items; measure gate accuracy and the quality loss on misrouted items.

claim: On ill-structured or less-structured tasks, a short list of named heuristic steps with NO worked example can improve strong models: Narration-of-Thought removed stakeholder collapse (15-31% to under 1%) with each step carrying its own effect; a patent-drafting step list helped GPT-4o (+5.2 human points) but only when followed silently (explicit text 2.2 points lower). Outcomes are trace features or small human samples, not verified decision quality.
agent_test: Skill-steps only vs example only vs both, on dilemma and design items, judged for answer quality at equal tokens; steps hidden vs written.

claim: For strong reasoning models, a near-identical worked example can mislead (the model copies steps); turning the example into a stated principle first and then solving without the example in view helped (GPT-4.1 AIME'25 34.0 to 48.0; open-ended sets gain only 0-2 points on small models, 57.68 to 68.40 on one 14B model). Skill-level abstraction beats topic-level content.
agent_test: Compare example-in-context vs principle-only vs both on open items.

claim: More examples is not better. On a structured classification task accuracy peaks at about 5-20 selected examples then declines (model-specific); for reasoning-distilled models one-shot CoT beat five-shot. No dose-response data exists for open-form tasks or for distant vs near examples.
agent_test: Dose test 0, 1, 3, 5 examples, near vs distant, on open items.

claim: Open-ended output is homogeneous within and across models (same-model similarity above 0.8 in 79% of cases; cross-model 71-82%), so sampling several models does not give real variety. Restoring variety needs structure in the request: sequential regeneration with earlier outputs shown matched 8 human writers on 3 models; system-prompt creativity requests and paraphrase barely helped; more reasoning effort in o3 lowered diversity.
agent_test: At equal tokens compare parallel sampling, direction stratification, verbalized sampling and sequential regeneration on novelty and judged quality.

claim: The benefit of a scaffold depends on the model's baseline, but not always in one direction: guidance helped strong models and cost weak ones up to 13.1 points on ill-structured items (Li 2026); self-reflection helped most models on IFEval but hurt 1.5B/1B models; on math, CoT gave larger relative gains for 32B on hard sets and for 1.5B on easy sets. No test uses an ill-structured task with a clean expertise-reversal design.
agent_test: Run the same open-mode scaffold on two model sizes and report where it flips from help to harm.
